capabilities: Upload images by drag and drop, paste, right-click, or file selection
Fetch remote images and re-upload them to the image bed
Batch upload all images in the current note and replace their links
Name files, folders, and backups with placeholder templates
Capture photos from the mobile camera or gallery
disambiguation: Not an image bed server itself; it is a client that uploads to a CloudFlare ImgBed instance you configure.
extras: Channel table notes limits: Telegram needs chunking above 20MB, Discord above 10MB, and Cloudflare R2 is billed after a 10GB free tier. API details are deferred to CloudFlare ImgBed's official documentation.
problem: Images pasted or dropped into notes stay in the vault, with no way to push them to a self-hosted image bed and swap in remote links.

relations.evidence: An Obsidian plugin for uploading images to CloudFlare ImgBed

requires.name: CloudFlare ImgBed auth code or API token

summary: Uploads images from Obsidian to a CloudFlare ImgBed instance and inserts the returned Markdown image links.
